title: A Legal Approach to Hate Speech – Operationalizing the EU’s Legal Framework against the Expression of Hatred as an NLP Task
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measures the ability to classify social media posts as legally punishable hate speech according to the EU Framework Decision, which explicitly includes hate speech directed at groups defined by their religion.
findings: The study operationalized the EU's legal definition of hate speech, which protects religious groups like Muslims and Jews, into an annotation scheme and dataset. Automated models (GBERT-base) found the task of directly predicting punishability challenging (F1 score of .39), but a subtask approach (identifying target group and conduct separately) yielded a comparable F1 score (.42) with better transparency. Models were more successful at identifying that a protected group was targeted (F1 up to .83) than in determining the final legal status of the post, with 'Muslims' and 'Jews' being distinct categories in the dataset.
